question: What is the distance between the pole and focus of a spherical mirror?
solution:
The correct answer is __**R/2**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **distance between the pole and the focus of a spherical mirror** is known as the **focal length**.

• Therefore, the correct distance between the pole and the focus of a spherical mirror is R2" id="MathJax-Element-5-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">R2 \frac{R}{2}.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A spherical mirror can be either concave or convex.
 
• In a **concave mirror**, the **focus is located on the same side as the object**, whereas, in a **convex mirror, the focus is located on the opposite side**.
 
• The radius of curvature (R) of a spherical mirror is the distance from the mirror's surface to its center of curvature.
 
• Understanding the relationship between the focal length and the radius of curvature is crucial in various optical applications and calculations.
